Gold slips as Warsh repricing, Hormuz oil spike lift rate risk - Kitco AM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold prices are lower and spot silver prices are firmer in early U.S. trading Monday, as traders weighed higher September Fed-hike odds and a renewed Strait of Hormuz oil shock against defensive demand tied to fresh U.S.-Iran escalation. At the time of writing, spot gold was trading near $4,438.20 an ounce, down 0.36%, while spot silver was trading at $66.860, up 0.91% on the session. The latest positioning remains defined by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s hawkish Jackson Hole message and a data-heavy week ahead. Futures-implied odds of a September rate hike were near 60% Monday, after Warsh’s speech pushed the two-year Treasury yield nearly 12 basis points higher Friday. The two-year yield dipped to about 4.325% in early Monday trade, but the move only trimmed Friday’s surge rather than reversing it. The next rate tests are Tuesday’s JOLTS job openings and ISM manufacturing data, Wednesday’s ADP employment report, Thursday’s jobless claims and ISM services data, and Friday’s August payrolls report. Gold remains caught between the rate shock and geopolitical bid. Friday’s selloff broke the metal below the 200-day moving average and put $4,396 back in focus in the latest technical setup, but Monday’s renewed Gulf risk has limited follow-through selling. Silver is trading better after bouncing from the $65.63 to $65.64 support area, but it remains below its short-term moving averages, leaving the rebound vulnerable unless buyers can clear the $67.75 to $68.40 resistance band.
